youtube channel:
Usage: socialscrape youtube channel [options]

YouTube - Channel Details

Options:
  --channelId [channelId]  YouTube channel ID. Can pass a channelId, handle or
                           url (e.g. UC-9-kyTW8ZkZNDHQJ6FgpwQ)
  --handle [handle]        YouTube channel handle. Can pass a channelId, handle
                           or url (e.g. ThePatMcAfeeShow)
  --url [url]              YouTube channel URL. Can pass a channelId, handle or
                           url (e.g. https://www.youtube.com/@ThePatMcAfeeShow)
  --cache-max-age <value>  If we have a response in the cache that is this many
                           days old or newer, return the cached response with
                           "cached": true and a "cached_at" timestamp.
                           Otherwise, scrape a live result. (e.g. 7d)
                           (1d|3d|7d|14d|30d)
  -h, --help               display help for command
youtube channel-videos:
Usage: socialscrape youtube channel-videos [options]

  --sort <value>                             Sort by latest or popular (e.g. latest) (latest|popular)
  --continuationToken [continuationToken]    Continuation token to get more videos. Get 'continuationToken' from previous response. (e.g. 4qmFsgKrCBIYVUNkRkpXVWE0M3NtUm00SXBIQnB)
  --is-paid-promotions [is-paid-promotions]  Set to 'true' to search YouTube's public paid product placement / sponsorship / endorsement search surface. This returns normal YouTube videos where the creator declared paid promotion. Cannot be combined with filter, uploadDate, sortBy, type, duration, or includeExtras.
  --includeExtras [includeExtras]            This will get you the like + comment count and the description. To get the full details of the video, use the /v1/youtube/video endpoint. Honestly, if you use this param, the error rate is higher. We might deprecate this param in the future.

youtube search:
Usage: socialscrape youtube search [options]

Options:

  --type <value>                             Type of content to search for (e.g. videos) (videos|shorts|channels|playlists)

  --continuationToken [continuationToken]    Continuation token to get more videos. Get 'continuationToken' from previous response. (e.g. 4qmFsgKrCBIYVUNkRkpXVWE0M3NtUm00SXBIQnB)
  --includeExtras [includeExtras]            This will get you the like + comment count and the description. To get the full details of the video, use the /v1/youtube/video endpoint. *This will slow down the response slightly.*

youtube video-transcript:
Usage: socialscrape youtube video-transcript [options]

YouTube - Transcript

Options:
  --url <url>              YouTube video or short URL (e.g.
                           https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bjVIDXPP7Uk)
  --language [language]    Language code, ie 'en', 'es', 'fr' or 'en-US'.
                           Overrides the default track selection unless
                           original_audio=true. If omitted, prefers captions
                           matching the original spoken language when YouTube
                           identifies the original audio. If that metadata is
                           unavailable or ambiguous, prefers an auto-generated
                           caption, otherwise the first caption track. If the
                           requested or identified original language has no
                           matching captions, the transcript will be null. (e.g.
                           en)
  --original-audio         Set to true to return captions only in the original
                           spoken language identified by YouTube. Takes
                           precedence over language. If the original audio
                           cannot be reliably identified or has no matching
                           captions, transcript, transcript_only_text, and
                           language are null. a returned transcript Omit or set
                           to false for the existing default selection.
  --cache-max-age <value>  If we have a response in the cache that is this many
                           days old or newer, return the cached response with
                           "cached": true and a "cached_at" timestamp.
                           Otherwise, scrape a live result. (e.g. 7d)
                           (1d|3d|7d|14d|30d)
  -h, --help               display help for command
